title: Dynamic critical exponent of the Yang--Lee edge singularity at three loops
authors: Loran Ts. Adzhemyan, Diana A. Davletbaeva, Daniil A. Evdokimov, Mikhail V. Kompaniets
abstract: We compute the dynamic critical exponent $z$ of the Yang--Lee edge singularity in relaxational dynamics using perturbative renormalization-group methods to the three-loop order. The calculation combines diagram reduction, analytic two-loop evaluation via parametric integration with hyperlogarithms, and numerical evaluation of three-loop integrals using the Sector Decomposition method. The perturbative series obtained is resummed using Padé and Padé-Borel-Leroy methods to produce estimates of $z$ in various spatial dimensions. The resulting values are consistent with previous perturbative and functional renormalization-group calculations.
summary: This paper calculates the dynamic critical exponent for the Yang–Lee edge singularity using high-order perturbative renormalization group theory. The methodology is highly technical, involving diagram reduction and multi-loop integration techniques like Sector Decomposition. It provides a robust estimate of $z$ by resumming the perturbative series to three loops, confirming consistency with established theoretical benchmarks.
main_problem: The primary goal is computing the dynamic critical exponent ($z$) associated with the Yang–Lee edge singularity (YLES) in relaxational dynamics.
main_result: The authors obtain a three-loop estimate for $z$ using advanced resummation techniques, finding results consistent with previous perturbative and functional renormalization group calculations across various spatial dimensions.
method: The calculation employs perturbative Renormalization Group (RG) methods, combining diagram reduction, analytic two-loop evaluation via parametric integration with hyperlogarithms, and numerical three-loop integral evaluation using Sector Decomposition.
model_or_system: The study models critical dynamics using a scalar field theory exhibiting an imaginary coupling constant ($i g_0$), described by a Langevin-type formulation (Model A in Hohenberg-Halperin classification).
key_observables: Dynamic critical exponent ($z$), renormalization constants ($Z_i$), and the running coupling constant $u$.
important_parameters: Spatial dimensions ($d$), loop order (up to three loops), and tuning parameters for resummation techniques.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that an imaginary fixed point can control real infrared asymptotic scaling behavior, and it relies on advanced mathematical tools like hyperlogarithms and sector decomposition for convergence.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the indices of one- and two-loop time versions after diagram reduction; Table II summarizes the final resummed estimates for $z$ across dimensions $d=1$ to $d=5$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the formalism by first addressing the complexity of dynamic diagrams, applying advanced renormalization techniques (BPHZ-like schemes), and finally presenting the results through multi-loop calculations followed by rigorous resummation using Padé and PBL methods.
why_interesting: While focused on critical dynamics rather than AMO systems directly, the sophisticated use of RG theory, diagrammatic techniques, and advanced summation methods (hyperlogarithms) represents state-of-the-art theoretical physics applicable to analyzing non-equilibrium quantum many-body systems.
